clue.text: Appropriate face for 19 24 21's creation …

definitions.note: 19, 24 and 21 together spell Oliver Postgate, the children's television maker whose creations are the theme

parts.note: to bag something is to appropriate or seize it
puss is slang for a face

explanation.surface: A mock reverent remark on the right expression for a famous puppet maker's work, trailing on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references 19, 24 and 21 give OLIVER POST GATE: Oliver Postgate made gentle British children's TV programmes in the 1960s and 70s. Bagpuss was his saggy cloth cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpuss, the baggy cloth cat of the 1974 children's series, was made by Oliver Postgate with Peter Firmin.

clue.text: Stage directors have seats on them

definitions.meaning: the theatre stage is called the ..., as in treading the ...
company directors sit on a board of management

explanation.surface: Theatre directors sit on platforms or chairs placed on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage directors' reads as one theatrical job; it splits into the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre stage is called the boards, and a company's directors sit on its governing boards.

clue.text: Good boy, oddly ignored, eyes girl

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: with the odd letters skipped, only the even letters of the word eyes are kept

explanation.surface: A well-behaved boy, strangely overlooked, looks at a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly ignored' looks like it describes the boy, but it acts on 'eyes', keeping its 2nd and 4th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a female given name, an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Fluid put on patio? Not altogether

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A liquid is spread on a patio, but not fully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' looks like a noun for something poured, but it is the anagram signal for PUT ON PATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true only partially, to a limited degree, holds not altogether, short of completely.

clue.text: Shakespeare's will is retained by Marshal Tito

definitions.note: the archaic second-person form of shall, as Shakespeare would write it

indicators.note: being retained by means held within, so the letters sit inside Marshal Tito

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean will has been kept by the Yugoslav leader Marshal Tito.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as a testament but is the verb; the old form for 'you will' runs across MARSHAL TITO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou shalt is the archaic form for you shall or will, typical of Shakespearean English.

clue.text: … one of 19 24 21's creations that might be dropped

definitions.meaning: the ... were Oliver Postgate's knitted, whistling moon creatures
to drop a ... is to make an embarrassing blunder

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, it pictures one of the puppet maker's works being let fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is a gaffe one 'drops', and the Clangers were Postgate's knitted moon-dwelling puppets.

clue.text: Authorisation required for this sort of sale?

definitions.meaning: official permission, as for security access or a plane's take-off

definitions.text: required for this sort of sale
definitions.meaning: a sale held to empty a shop of its stock

explanation.surface: A question about what permission a certain type of sale needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Security or take-off permission is called clearance, and a clearance sale empties stock.

clue.text: Fervent giant-killer loses his head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the name is taken off

parts.note: David killed the giant Goliath in the Bible

explanation.surface: A passionate slayer of giants is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of DAVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager and enthusiastic, so keen and passionate.

clue.text: Mournful composer crossing Alsace?

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the composer's name goes round the wine

parts.note: Edvard Grieg, the Norwegian composer
Alsace, a French wine region, stands for wine, French vin

explanation.surface: A sad composer travels across the French region of Alsace.
explanation.walkthrough: VIN is French for wine, and Alsace is a French wine; GRIEG straddles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone grieving is sorrowful and in mourning after a loss.

clue.text: Kit appears in show with animals — he's no friend of Othello

indicators.note: appearing in means standing inside, so the kit word goes within the show

parts.note: a rodeo is a show of riding bucking horses and roping cattle
a rig is a set of equipment, kit

explanation.surface: Equipment appears in an animal show, with a nod to a villain against Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit' looks like a person's name but is equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo, Iago's dupe in Othello, plots against the Moor and is no friend to him.

clue.text: 27 or 8, separately?

definitions.meaning: Laertes and Roderigo, the answers at 27 and 8, are each a role in a Shakespeare play, read as two words
taken ... means set aside from each other

explanation.surface: A terse query asking whether two Shakespearean characters belong apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer says 'a role', which Laertes (in Hamlet) and Roderigo (in Othello) both are.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept away from one another are held separately, in distinct places; and each character is a single theatrical role.

clue.text: In a mess, if iced tea turned into vinegar

indicators.note: something in a mess is jumbled up, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spoilt glass of iced tea has gone sour like vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a mess' rearranges IF ICED TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To acetify is to convert into acetic acid, the sour substance of vinegar.

clue.text: One may be charged with crime after needing a drink

indicators.note: the crime word follows the thirst word in the answer

parts.note: someone thirsty is dry
battery is the crime of unlawful physical assault

explanation.surface: A suspect is charged with an offence committed after a drinking urge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks legal, but it means filled with electricity: a dry battery is a cell that holds a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cell battery is something that is electrically charged to store power.

definitions.note: Oliver Postgate's engine, from the series about a small Welsh railway locomotive

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle of numbers and cross-references asking which of Postgate's machines is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 looks like a reference to 4-down, but it is just the number in Roman numerals. 20 is ENGINE: Ivor the Engine was Postgate's Welsh steam locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor was the little green Welsh steam locomotive in Postgate's series Ivor the Engine.

clue.text: You must be on base — you look likely to be frightening

parts.note: thee is an old form of you
base means low and vile
ye is an old plural of you

explanation.surface: A soldier must stay on base, warned that they seem scary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' reads as a military camp; it means low, vile.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent glare believed to cast a curse, a frightening look.

clue.text: Time he brought in drinks for 19 24 21's creation

indicators.note: the time and he letters are carried inside the two drinks

parts.note: a noggin is a small measure of drink and nog is a strong ale or eggnog
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man arrives carrying drinks while time passes, for the puppet maker's show.
explanation.walkthrough: The two drinks sit either side of T and HE. Noggin the Nog was Postgate's gentle Norse saga for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Noggin the Nog, a kindly Viking king, starred in Postgate and Firmin's animated sagas from 1959.

clue.text: Frank Ifield's first — see gulls gathering round

indicators.note: the letters milling and gathering round each other suggests a jumbled rearrangement
first takes only the opening letter of the singer's name

explanation.surface: The singer Frank Ifield watches gulls gathering around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' reads as Frank Ifield, the singer, but is the definition; rearrange I, SEE and GULLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means open and honest, and a guileless person is without deceit.

clue.text: American revolutionary chewed garlic? Such spirit!

definitions.note: an adjective clue: surgical spirit is the antiseptic alcohol

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the American letters are read backwards

parts.note: US is short for American, the United States

indicators.note: chewed means mashed up, so the letters of garlic are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American rebel chomping garlic shows remarkable spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like courage; surgical spirit is the British name for rubbing alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical spirit is the British name for methylated antiseptic alcohol used to clean skin.

clue.text: One leaving Old Tolbooth without penalty?

definitions.meaning: the Old Tolbooth was Edinburgh's prison, so a man released from it would be a Scot set at liberty

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of an old Scottish jail unpunished.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Tolbooth was Edinburgh's old jail; a released prisoner there would be a Scot freed.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape punishment entirely; scot was originally a tax.

clue.text: Don, seducer in trouble, may be ignored

indicators.note: the phrase in trouble, read as words in disorder, signals a rearrangement of the letters before it

explanation.surface: A womanising Don in difficulty might be disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' belongs to the fodder, not the indicator: rearrange DONSEDUCERIN, with 'trouble' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unconsidered has been left out of thought, disregarded or overlooked.

clue.text: Goldsmith's musical

definitions.meaning: the first name of ... Goldsmith, the Irish author
the Lionel Bart stage show based on ... Twist

explanation.surface: A jeweller's stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goldsmith' reads as a jeweller but is the 18th-century writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith wrote She Stoops to Conquer, and Lionel Bart's Oliver! is a famous stage musical.

clue.text: Car part, say, overlapping 9

parts.note: a motor is an example of a car part, and 9-across reads a part, so it is a car's 'a part', overlapping that entry in the grid

explanation.surface: A component of a car, perhaps, crossing over a numbered piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a car part, and also the engine of 12-across, Ivor the Engine; 'overlapping 9' plays on 9-across, APART.
explanation.definitionFit: The motor is the chief working part under a car's bonnet that drives it.

clue.text: Gun carriage finally makes an entrance

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word carriage

explanation.surface: A gun carriage at last arrives at a grand doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun carriage' reads as one military thing; it splits into GAT and the end of carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is a hinged barrier forming a way in through a wall or fence.

clue.text: A shot writer nurses one left at home

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the writer holds the one inside it

parts.note: a pencil is a writing implement
I is the Roman numeral for one
in means at home

explanation.surface: A writer looks after a sick person at home with an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests a person, but it is the implement PENCIL, which takes I after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is an injection, and penicillin is an antibiotic often given that way.

clue.text: Faith is supported by short Asian monk

indicators.note: in a down clue the first word sits on top of the second, held up by it
short means cut off, so the final letter of the monk is dropped

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: Religious belief is upheld by a monk of small stature from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: IS stands above LAM, the clipped LAMA, as 'supported by' says in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic religion of Muslims, a world faith.

clue.text: Letters from the office

definitions.meaning: an office is a job or position held

explanation.surface: Correspondence sent from a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is called the post, and a job or appointment is a post.

clue.text: Opening covered with pink material

indicators.note: the opening is enclosed by the pink word on both sides

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-orange colour
a pore is a tiny opening in skin

explanation.surface: A gap in a garment is patched over with pink fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like fabric, but here it is the adjective for physical, bodily.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily or physical, belonging to the material world rather than the spiritual.

clue.text: Novice upset about missing conclusion

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of novice are rearranged
missing tells us the letter for about is left out of the rearranged word

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A beginner is upset at not finding an ending.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the C (circa, 'about') from NOVICE as 'missing' instructs, then 'upset' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is the short closing stanza of a poem, so its formal conclusion.

clue.text: Dennis accepts rate reform — he's no friend of Hamlet

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the name holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: Les Dennis is a British comedian and game-show host

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Dennis welcomes a change to a tax rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dennis' looks like a surname to keep whole, but it points to the British TV entertainer Les Dennis, so it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes fights Hamlet in the final duel with a poisoned blade, avenging his father Polonius.

clue.text: Marilyn has church for old tennis player

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the church letters take the place of the old letter

parts.note: Marilyn Monroe, the film star
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A film star joins a church, standing in for a former sports figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old tennis player' looks like the definition, but 'old' is O, which CE (Church of England) replaces in MONROE.
explanation.definitionFit: John McEnroe is a retired American tennis champion, a Wimbledon winner of the 1980s.
